basic_info.title: Trembr: Exploring Road Networks for Trajectory Representation Learning
basic_info.venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology (TIST) 2020, Vol. 11, Issue 1, Article 10

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Trembr uses an RNN (not a transformer) encoder-decoder and has no graph neural network: Road2Vec learns road-segment embeddings from network topology in a word2vec-style manner rather than via a GNN, so the semantic_vectorized_transformer_encoder pillar is unmet. There is no RL agent and no latent-space decision-making.
gap_analysis.reasoning: An early self-supervised reconstruction approach (Traj2Vec RNN encoder-decoder reconstructing road sequences plus travel time, with Road2Vec embeddings injecting road-type/traffic features); it is label-free but pre-transformer and pre-RL, covering only one pillar.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Foundational reference showing road-network-constrained, label-free trajectory embeddings; predates transformer/RL methods so mainly historical/motivational for the thesis.
